ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.professional_id ,  T1.role_code ,  T1.first_name FROM Professionals AS T1 JOIN Treatments AS T2 ON T1.professional_id  =  T2.professional_id GROUP BY T1.professional_id HAVING count(*)  >=  2

prefix_hints.sol_2: I join each professional to their treatments through the shared professional id: `FROM Professionals AS T1 JOIN Treatments AS T2 ON T1.professional_id  =  T2.professional_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group the joined rows by professional so each treatment count is calculated per professional: `FROM Professionals AS T1 JOIN Treatments AS T2 ON T1.professional_id  =  T2.professional_id GROUP BY T1.professional_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I retain the professional groups containing at least two treatments: `FROM Professionals AS T1 JOIN Treatments AS T2 ON T1.professional_id  =  T2.professional_id GROUP BY T1.professional_id HAVING count(*)  >=  2`.

prefix_hints.sol_5: I project that country's name, completing the query: `SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN religion AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country GROUP BY T1.Name ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT T2.Name) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Name the oldest employee who is working on night shift. How old is the employee?

Evidence:
working on night shift refers to ShiftID = 3; oldest employee refers to min(BirthDate); age = 2022-year(BirthDate)+1
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.FirstName, T1.LastName , STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', BirthDate) FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE T3.ShiftId = 3 ORDER BY STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', BirthDate) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with `Person` and join each person to the corresponding employee record by business entity id: `FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join the employee’s department history so the assigned shift is available: `FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I keep the department-history records for the night shift, identified by ShiftId 3: `FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE T3.ShiftId = 3`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I calculate age from the current year and birth year, then sort descending so the oldest night-shift employee comes first: `FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE T3.ShiftId = 3 ORDER BY STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', BirthDate) DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I return that employee’s first name, last name, and calculated age, limiting the result to the oldest one: `SELECT T1.FirstName, T1.LastName , STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', BirthDate) FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE T3.ShiftId = 3 ORDER BY STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', BirthDate) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:

ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.Name, T2.Name, T2.Percentage FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T1.Name = ( SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country GROUP BY T1.Name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.Name) DESC LIMIT 1 ) GROUP BY T1.Name, T2.Name, T2.Percentage

prefix_hints.sol_1: I join each country to its ethnic groups through the country code so I can count the groups associated with each full country name: `SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I group those joined rows by full country name to obtain one group per country: `SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country GROUP BY T1.Name`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I order the countries by their ethnic-group count in descending order and retain the country with the highest count: `SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country GROUP BY T1.Name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.Name) DESC LIMIT 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I use that result to filter the outer country-to-ethnic-group join to the selected country: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T1.Name = ( SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country GROUP BY T1.Name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.Name) DESC LIMIT 1 )`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I return the country's full name with every ethnic-group name and percentage, grouping by those projected values to complete the query: `SELECT T1.Name, T2.Name, T2.Percentage FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T1.Name = ( SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country GROUP BY T1.Name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.Name) DESC LIMIT 1 ) GROUP BY T1.Name, T2.Name, T2.Percentage`.

Question:
Name all countries in which have border with Bulgaria.

Evidence:
Bulgaria is a country name
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T3.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN borders AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country1 INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T3.Code = T2.Country2 WHERE T1.Name = 'Bulgaria'

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with the country table so I can identify Bulgaria by name and access its country code: `FROM country AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join Bulgaria's code to the first country code in the borders table: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN borders AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country1`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I join the second border code back to country so I can retrieve the neighboring country's name: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN borders AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country1 INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T3.Code = T2.Country2`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I restrict the first country to Bulgaria: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN borders AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country1 INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T3.Code = T2.Country2 WHERE T1.Name = 'Bulgaria'`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I return the names of the countries on the other side of Bulgaria's borders: `SELECT T3.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN borders AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country1 INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T3.Code = T2.Country2 WHERE T1.Name = 'Bulgaria'`.

Calculate the total points scored by team ID ANA and list down the coashes of the team.

Evidence:

ground_truth.answer: SELECT SUM(T2.Pts), T1.coachID FROM Coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T2.tmID = T1.tmID WHERE T2.tmID = 'ANA' GROUP BY T1.coachID

prefix_hints.sol_1: I link each coaching record to its team record through the shared team ID so the coach and team points are available together: `FROM Coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T2.tmID = T1.tmID`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I restrict the joined records to team ANA: `FROM Coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T2.tmID = T1.tmID WHERE T2.tmID = 'ANA'`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group the records by coach so the points total is reported alongside each coach ID: `FROM Coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T2.tmID = T1.tmID WHERE T2.tmID = 'ANA' GROUP BY T1.coachID`.

prefix_hints.sol_2: I join each order to its items so the ordered quantities are available: `FROM customers AS t1 JOIN customer_orders AS t2 ON t1.customer_id  =  t2.customer_id JOIN order_items AS t3 ON t2.order_id  =  t3.order_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group the matched order items by customer name so I can total each customer's quantities: `FROM customers AS t1 JOIN customer_orders AS t2 ON t1.customer_id  =  t2.customer_id JOIN order_items AS t3 ON t2.order_id  =  t3.order_id GROUP BY t1.customer_name`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I sort the customer groups by their summed order quantity in descending order, placing the largest total first: `FROM customers AS t1 JOIN customer_orders AS t2 ON t1.customer_id  =  t2.customer_id JOIN order_items AS t3 ON t2.order_id  =  t3.order_id GROUP BY t1.customer_name ORDER BY sum(t3.order_quantity) DESC`.

Question:
Which team(s) had 90% games won. List the coach ID for the team and year played.

Evidence:
team with 90% games won refers to Divide (won, games) > 0.9
ground_truth.answer: SELECT DISTINCT T2.name, T1.year, T1.coachID FROM coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID WHERE CAST(T2.won AS REAL) * 100 / T2.games > 90

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with the coaching records, which provide the coach ID and season year: `FROM coaches AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join each coaching record to its team so the team name, wins, and games are available: `FROM coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I keep teams whose wins represent more than 90 percent of their games, casting wins to REAL for division: `FROM coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID WHERE CAST(T2.won AS REAL) * 100 / T2.games > 90`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I select the team name, year, and coach ID, using DISTINCT to remove repeated result rows: `SELECT DISTINCT T2.name, T1.year, T1.coachID FROM coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID WHERE CAST(T2.won AS REAL) * 100 / T2.games > 90`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: This completes the query: `SELECT DISTINCT T2.name, T1.year, T1.coachID FROM coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID WHERE CAST(T2.won AS REAL) * 100 / T2.games > 90`.

Evidence:
most order refers to Max(OrderQty);

prefix_hints.sol_5: I retain the first five products in that ranking, completing the query: `SELECT T1.Name FROM Product AS T1 INNER JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID GROUP BY T1.Name ORDER BY SUM(T2.OrderQty) DESC LIMIT 0, 5`.

Question:
Among the countries with a population of under 1000000, how many of them have over 2 languages?
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T2.Country FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN language AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T1.Population < 1000000 GROUP BY T2.Country HAVING COUNT(T1.Name) > 2

prefix_hints.sol_1: Country populations and languages are in separate tables, so I join `country` to `language` using the country code: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN language AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I restrict the joined rows to countries whose population is under 1000000: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN language AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T1.Population < 1000000`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group the remaining language rows by country so each country's languages can be counted: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN language AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T1.Population < 1000000 GROUP BY T2.Country`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I retain country groups having more than two language records: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN language AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T1.Population < 1000000 GROUP BY T2.Country HAVING COUNT(T1.Name) > 2`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I return the country identifier for every qualifying group: `SELECT T2.Country FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN language AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T1.Population < 1000000 GROUP BY T2.Country HAVING COUNT(T1.Name) > 2`.

ground_truth.answer: SELECT T2.name FROM TeamsSC AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year GROUP BY T2.name ORDER BY SUM(T1.W) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_4: I order the teams by their summed Stanley Cup wins in descending order: `FROM TeamsSC AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year GROUP BY T2.name ORDER BY SUM(T1.W) DESC`.

ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.name_first ,  T1.name_last ,  T2.player_id FROM player AS T1 JOIN manager_award AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id GROUP BY T2.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1;

prefix_hints.sol_1: I link each manager-award record to the corresponding player so the manager’s name is available: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN manager_award AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I group the award records by manager id so each manager’s awards can be counted together: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN manager_award AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id GROUP BY T2.player_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I order those manager groups by their number of award records in descending order: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN manager_award AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id GROUP BY T2.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I keep the first group, which is the manager with the most awards: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN manager_award AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id GROUP BY T2.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I project that manager’s first name, last name, and player id to complete the query: `SELECT T1.name_first ,  T1.name_last ,  T2.player_id FROM player AS T1 JOIN manager_award AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id GROUP BY T2.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1;`.

Question:
What's the weight of the player who had the most Power Play Goals in the 21st century?

Evidence:
21st century refers to year >2000; Power play goals refers to PPG
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.weight FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.year > 2000 GROUP BY T1.playerID, T1.weight ORDER BY SUM(T2.PPG) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_2: I restrict the scoring records to the 21st century, defined here as years after 2000: `FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.year > 2000`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group by player and weight so each player's power-play goals can be totaled across seasons: `FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.year > 2000 GROUP BY T1.playerID, T1.weight`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I sort the players by their summed PPG in descending order and keep the top one: `FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.year > 2000 GROUP BY T1.playerID, T1.weight ORDER BY SUM(T2.PPG) DESC LIMIT 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I return that top player's weight: `SELECT T1.weight FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.year > 2000 GROUP BY T1.playerID, T1.weight ORDER BY SUM(T2.PPG) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
What are the monthly rentals of student addresses in Texas state?

prefix_hints.sol_3: I restrict the joined addresses to those in Texas: `FROM Addresses AS T1 JOIN Student_Addresses AS T2 ON T1.address_id  =  T2.address_id WHERE T1.state_province_county  =  "Texas"`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I project the monthly rental from each matching student-address record: `SELECT T2.monthly_rental FROM Addresses AS T1 JOIN Student_Addresses AS T2 ON T1.address_id  =  T2.address_id WHERE T1.state_province_county  =  "Texas"`.

Question:
Please provide contact details of all Marketing Managers. State their name and phone number.

Evidence:
Marketing Manager is a job title
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.FirstName, T1.LastName, T2.PhoneNumber FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN PersonPhone AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Employee AS T3 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE T3.JobTitle = 'Marketing Manager'

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with `Person`, which contains the first and last names: `FROM Person AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join `PersonPhone` by business entity so each person is associated with a phone number: `FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN PersonPhone AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I then join `Employee` on the same identifier to make the employee job title available: `FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN PersonPhone AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Employee AS T3 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I keep employees whose job title is Marketing Manager: `FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN PersonPhone AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Employee AS T3 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE T3.JobTitle = 'Marketing Manager'`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I return each matching employee's first name, last name, and phone number: `SELECT T1.FirstName, T1.LastName, T2.PhoneNumber FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN PersonPhone AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Employee AS T3 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE T3.JobTitle = 'Marketing Manager'`.

Question:
Calculate the average age of employee in each department and state which department has the youngest employees.

Evidence:
Average = Divide(Sum(Substract(year(@today),year(BirthDate))),Count(BusinessEntityID) by each Department ID; youngest employee refers to Min(BirthDate);
ground_truth.answer: SELECT STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.BirthDate) + 1 , T3.Name FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 USING (BusinessEntityID) INNER JOIN Department AS T3 USING (DepartmentID) ORDER BY T1.BirthDate DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with employees so I can use each employee's birth date and business entity id: `FROM Employee AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I connect each employee to the employee's department history through the shared BusinessEntityID: `FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 USING (BusinessEntityID)`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I then join Department through DepartmentID so the corresponding department name is available: `FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 USING (BusinessEntityID) INNER JOIN Department AS T3 USING (DepartmentID)`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: The youngest employee has the latest birth date, so I sort birth dates descending and retain the first row: `FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 USING (BusinessEntityID) INNER JOIN Department AS T3 USING (DepartmentID) ORDER BY T1.BirthDate DESC LIMIT 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I calculate that employee's age from the current year, add one as specified, and return it with the department name: `SELECT STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.BirthDate) + 1 , T3.Name FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 USING (BusinessEntityID) INNER JOIN Department AS T3 USING (DepartmentID) ORDER BY T1.BirthDate DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Which constitutional monarchy nations saw the greatest growth in the number of organizations after 1907?

Nation refers to country; Information of growth appears in the column Established
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN organization AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN politics AS T3 ON T3.Country = T2.Country WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.Established) > '1907' AND T3.Government = 'constitutional monarchy' GROUP BY T1.Name ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT T2.Name) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_1: I link each country to its organizations through the country code: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN organization AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I add politics on the same country code so the form of government is available: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN organization AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN politics AS T3 ON T3.Country = T2.Country`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I restrict the organizations to those established after 1907 and the countries to constitutional monarchies: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN organization AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN politics AS T3 ON T3.Country = T2.Country WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.Established) > '1907' AND T3.Government = 'constitutional monarchy'`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I group by country name and rank the countries by their count of distinct organization names in descending order: `SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN organization AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN politics AS T3 ON T3.Country = T2.Country WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.Established) > '1907' AND T3.Government = 'constitutional monarchy' GROUP BY T1.Name ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT T2.Name) DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I keep only the highest-ranked country, completing the query: `SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN organization AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN politics AS T3 ON T3.Country = T2.Country WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.Established) > '1907' AND T3.Government = 'constitutional monarchy' GROUP BY T1.Name ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT T2.Name) DESC LIMIT 1`.

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from each claim and select its effective date: `SELECT t1.Effective_Date FROM claims AS t1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join settlements on the claim id so I can total the settlement amounts for each claim: `SELECT t1.Effective_Date FROM claims AS t1 JOIN settlements AS t2 ON t1.claim_id  =  t2.claim_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group the joined rows by claim so multiple settlements are combined for the same claim: `SELECT t1.Effective_Date FROM claims AS t1 JOIN settlements AS t2 ON t1.claim_id  =  t2.claim_id GROUP BY t1.claim_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I order the claim groups by their summed settlement amounts in descending order, placing the largest total first: `SELECT t1.Effective_Date FROM claims AS t1 JOIN settlements AS t2 ON t1.claim_id  =  t2.claim_id GROUP BY t1.claim_id ORDER BY sum(t2.settlement_amount) DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I retain only the first claim, which has the largest total settlement amount: `SELECT t1.Effective_Date FROM claims AS t1 JOIN settlements AS t2 ON t1.claim_id  =  t2.claim_id GROUP BY t1.claim_id ORDER BY sum(t2.settlement_amount) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Among the products that are both manufactured in house and salable, how many of them get over 10 reviews?

Evidence:
manufactured in house refers to MakeFlag = 1; salable product refers to FinishedGoodsFlag = 1; over 10 reviews refers to count(comments)>10
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T2.Name FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 USING (ProductID) WHERE T2.FinishedGoodsFlag = 1 AND T2.MakeFlag = 1 GROUP BY T2.Name ORDER BY COUNT(T1.COMMENTS) > 10

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from `ProductReview` because the review comments are counted there: `FROM ProductReview AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join each review to its product through the shared `ProductID` so I can access the product name and flags: `FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 USING (ProductID)`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I retain products that are salable and manufactured in house by requiring both flags to equal 1: `FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 USING (ProductID) WHERE T2.FinishedGoodsFlag = 1 AND T2.MakeFlag = 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I group the matched reviews by product name so `COUNT(T1.COMMENTS)` is calculated for each product: `FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 USING (ProductID) WHERE T2.FinishedGoodsFlag = 1 AND T2.MakeFlag = 1 GROUP BY T2.Name`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I select the grouped product names and order them by whether their comment count exceeds 10: `SELECT T2.Name FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 USING (ProductID) WHERE T2.FinishedGoodsFlag = 1 AND T2.MakeFlag = 1 GROUP BY T2.Name ORDER BY COUNT(T1.COMMENTS) > 10`.

Question:
What is the full name of the sales person who has the the highest commission percent received per sale?

Evidence:
commision percent received per sale refers to CommissionPct; highest commision percent received per sale refers to MAX(CommissionPcT); full name = FirstName+MiddleName+LastName;
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T2.FirstName, T2.MiddleName, T2.LastName FROM SalesPerson AS T1 INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID ORDER BY T1.CommissionPct DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_2: I join each salesperson to their person record so their name fields are available: `FROM SalesPerson AS T1 INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I sort the salespeople by commission percentage in descending order, placing the highest percentage first: `FROM SalesPerson AS T1 INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID ORDER BY T1.CommissionPct DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I retain only the first salesperson in that descending ranking: `FROM SalesPerson AS T1 INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID ORDER BY T1.CommissionPct DESC LIMIT 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I return that salesperson's first, middle, and last names: `SELECT T2.FirstName, T2.MiddleName, T2.LastName FROM SalesPerson AS T1 INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID ORDER BY T1.CommissionPct DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Among the vendors with maximum orders betweeen 500 to 750, which vendor has the 10th highest profit on net?

Evidence:
maximum orders refers to MaxOrderQty; MaxOrderQty BETWEEN '500' AND '750'; profit on net = SUBTRACT(LastReceiptCost, StandardPrice);
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T2.Name FROM ProductVendor AS T1 INNER JOIN Vendor AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.MaxOrderQty BETWEEN 500 AND 750 ORDER BY T1.LastReceiptCost - T1.StandardPrice DESC LIMIT 9, 1

prefix_hints.sol_2: I join `Vendor` on the shared business entity id so I can retrieve each vendor's name: `FROM ProductVendor AS T1 INNER JOIN Vendor AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I keep vendor-product records whose maximum order quantity is between 500 and 750: `FROM ProductVendor AS T1 INNER JOIN Vendor AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.MaxOrderQty BETWEEN 500 AND 750`.

prefix_hints.sol_5: I skip the first nine ranked records and return the tenth one: `SELECT T2.Name FROM ProductVendor AS T1 INNER JOIN Vendor AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.MaxOrderQty BETWEEN 500 AND 750 ORDER BY T1.LastReceiptCost - T1.StandardPrice DESC LIMIT 9, 1`.

prefix_hints.sol_5: I select the owner id and zip code, then keep only the first owner in that ordering: `SELECT T1.owner_id ,  T1.zip_code FROM Owners AS T1 JOIN Dogs AS T2 ON T1.owner_id  =  T2.owner_id JOIN Treatments AS T3 ON T2.dog_id  =  T3.dog_id GROUP BY T1.owner_id ORDER BY sum(T3.cost_of_treatment) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
For the on going assembly item Component ID No. 494, what's the Unit measure for it?

Evidence:
On going assembly item means the assembly item haven't been finished, therefore EndDate is null
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T2.Name FROM BillOfMaterials AS T1 INNER JOIN UnitMeasure AS T2 ON T1.UnitMeasureCode = T2.UnitMeasureCode WHERE T1.ComponentID = 494 AND T1.EndDate IS NULL GROUP BY T2.name

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with `BillOfMaterials`, which contains the component, completion date, and unit measure code: `FROM BillOfMaterials AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join `UnitMeasure` on the shared unit measure code so I can retrieve its descriptive name: `FROM BillOfMaterials AS T1 INNER JOIN UnitMeasure AS T2 ON T1.UnitMeasureCode = T2.UnitMeasureCode`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I restrict the rows to component 494 and identify an ongoing assembly by requiring a null end date: `FROM BillOfMaterials AS T1 INNER JOIN UnitMeasure AS T2 ON T1.UnitMeasureCode = T2.UnitMeasureCode WHERE T1.ComponentID = 494 AND T1.EndDate IS NULL`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I group by the unit measure name so the result has one row per matching measure: `FROM BillOfMaterials AS T1 INNER JOIN UnitMeasure AS T2 ON T1.UnitMeasureCode = T2.UnitMeasureCode WHERE T1.ComponentID = 494 AND T1.EndDate IS NULL GROUP BY T2.name`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I select the unit measure name, completing the query: `SELECT T2.Name FROM BillOfMaterials AS T1 INNER JOIN UnitMeasure AS T2 ON T1.UnitMeasureCode = T2.UnitMeasureCode WHERE T1.ComponentID = 494 AND T1.EndDate IS NULL GROUP BY T2.name`.

ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.Name, T1.Population * T2.Percentage FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T2.Name = 'Chinese' AND T2.Percentage > 70

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from `country`, which provides each country's name, code, and population: `FROM country AS T1`.

prefix_hints.sol_3: I restrict the joined rows to the Chinese ethnic group: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T2.Name = 'Chinese'`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I then keep countries where the Chinese percentage is greater than 70: `FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T2.Name = 'Chinese' AND T2.Percentage > 70`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I return each country name and multiply its population by the Chinese percentage as required: `SELECT T1.Name, T1.Population * T2.Percentage FROM country AS T1 INNER JOIN ethnicGroup AS T2 ON T1.Code = T2.Country WHERE T2.Name = 'Chinese' AND T2.Percentage > 70`.

Question:
List all the sales people in the Northwest US.

Evidence:
Northwest is name of SalesTerritory; US is the CountryRegionCode;
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T2.BusinessEntityID FROM SalesTerritory AS T1 INNER JOIN SalesPerson AS T2 ON T1.TerritoryID = T2.TerritoryID WHERE T1.Name = 'Northwest' AND T1.CountryRegionCode = 'US'

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from `SalesTerritory`, where the territory name and country code identify the requested region: `FROM SalesTerritory AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join `SalesPerson` on the shared territory ID to associate each territory with its sales people: `FROM SalesTerritory AS T1 INNER JOIN SalesPerson AS T2 ON T1.TerritoryID = T2.TerritoryID`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I restrict the joined rows to the Northwest sales territory: `FROM SalesTerritory AS T1 INNER JOIN SalesPerson AS T2 ON T1.TerritoryID = T2.TerritoryID WHERE T1.Name = 'Northwest'`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I further require the territory's country-region code to be US: `FROM SalesTerritory AS T1 INNER JOIN SalesPerson AS T2 ON T1.TerritoryID = T2.TerritoryID WHERE T1.Name = 'Northwest' AND T1.CountryRegionCode = 'US'`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I return the business entity ID of each matching salesperson: `SELECT T2.BusinessEntityID FROM SalesTerritory AS T1 INNER JOIN SalesPerson AS T2 ON T1.TerritoryID = T2.TerritoryID WHERE T1.Name = 'Northwest' AND T1.CountryRegionCode = 'US'`.

Question:
Show the name and distance of the aircrafts with more than 5000 distance and which at least 5 people have its certificate.
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T2.name FROM Certificate AS T1 JOIN Aircraft AS T2 ON T2.aid  =  T1.aid WHERE T2.distance  >  5000 GROUP BY T1.aid ORDER BY count(*)  >=  5

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from the certificate records, where each row associates a person with an aircraft: `FROM Certificate AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join each certificate to its aircraft so the aircraft name and distance are available: `FROM Certificate AS T1 JOIN Aircraft AS T2 ON T2.aid = T1.aid`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I retain aircraft whose distance is greater than 5000: `FROM Certificate AS T1 JOIN Aircraft AS T2 ON T2.aid = T1.aid WHERE T2.distance > 5000`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I group the certificate rows by aircraft so `count(*)` represents the number of people holding each aircraft's certificate: `FROM Certificate AS T1 JOIN Aircraft AS T2 ON T2.aid = T1.aid WHERE T2.distance > 5000 GROUP BY T1.aid`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I select the aircraft name and order the grouped results by whether the certificate count is at least five: `SELECT T2.name FROM Certificate AS T1 JOIN Aircraft AS T2 ON T2.aid = T1.aid WHERE T2.distance > 5000 GROUP BY T1.aid ORDER BY count(*) >= 5`.

What was the longest time that Lewis Hamilton had spent at a pit stop?

longest time refes to MAX(duration);
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.duration FROM pitStops AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 on T1.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE T2.forename = 'Lewis' AND T2.surname = 'Hamilton' ORDER BY T1.duration DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_1: Pit-stop durations are recorded in `pitStops`, so I start from that table: `FROM pitStops AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join the driver details through `driverId` so I can identify whose stop each duration belongs to: `FROM pitStops AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 on T1.driverId = T2.driverId`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I restrict the rows to Lewis Hamilton by matching both his forename and surname: `FROM pitStops AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 on T1.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE T2.forename = 'Lewis' AND T2.surname = 'Hamilton'`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I select the duration and sort it from longest to shortest: `SELECT T1.duration FROM pitStops AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 on T1.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE T2.forename = 'Lewis' AND T2.surname = 'Hamilton' ORDER BY T1.duration DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I keep the first sorted row to return his longest pit-stop time: `SELECT T1.duration FROM pitStops AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 on T1.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE T2.forename = 'Lewis' AND T2.surname = 'Hamilton' ORDER BY T1.duration DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
List all members and member type of the Islamic Development Bank.
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T2.Country, T2.Type FROM organization AS T1 INNER JOIN isMember AS T2 ON T1.Abbreviation = T2.Organization INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T2.Country = T3.Code WHERE T1.Name = 'Islamic Development Bank'

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from `organization`, where the bank name and abbreviation identify the requested organization: `FROM organization AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join its membership records by matching the organization abbreviation to the membership organization code: `FROM organization AS T1 INNER JOIN isMember AS T2 ON T1.Abbreviation = T2.Organization`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I connect each membership record to its country through the country code: `FROM organization AS T1 INNER JOIN isMember AS T2 ON T1.Abbreviation = T2.Organization INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T2.Country = T3.Code`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I restrict the organization to the Islamic Development Bank by its full name: `FROM organization AS T1 INNER JOIN isMember AS T2 ON T1.Abbreviation = T2.Organization INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T2.Country = T3.Code WHERE T1.Name = 'Islamic Development Bank'`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I return each member country code and its member type: `SELECT T2.Country, T2.Type FROM organization AS T1 INNER JOIN isMember AS T2 ON T1.Abbreviation = T2.Organization INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T2.Country = T3.Code WHERE T1.Name = 'Islamic Development Bank'`.

Question:
How much are the minimum orders of the vendors that are no longer used by the company?

Evidence:
vendors that are no longer used by the company refers to ActiveFlag = 0;
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T2.MinOrderQty FROM Vendor AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductVendor AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.ActiveFlag = 0 ORDER BY T2.MinOrderQty LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_1: Vendor status and minimum order quantities are in separate tables, so I join `Vendor` to `ProductVendor` on the shared business entity id: `FROM Vendor AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductVendor AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I restrict the joined rows to vendors that are no longer active: `FROM Vendor AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductVendor AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.ActiveFlag = 0`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I sort their minimum order quantities in ascending order so the smallest appears first: `FROM Vendor AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductVendor AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.ActiveFlag = 0 ORDER BY T2.MinOrderQty`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I retain only that first, smallest quantity: `FROM Vendor AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductVendor AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.ActiveFlag = 0 ORDER BY T2.MinOrderQty LIMIT 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I project the minimum order quantity, completing the query: `SELECT T2.MinOrderQty FROM Vendor AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductVendor AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.ActiveFlag = 0 ORDER BY T2.MinOrderQty LIMIT 1`.

ground_truth.answer: SELECT T2.name ,  T1.team_id_winner FROM postseason AS T1 JOIN team AS T2 ON T1.team_id_winner  =  T2.team_id_br WHERE T1.year  =  2008 GROUP BY T1.team_id_winner ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1;

prefix_hints.sol_1: I link each postseason winner to its team record so I can retrieve the team name: `FROM postseason AS T1 JOIN team AS T2 ON T1.team_id_winner  =  T2.team_id_br`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I restrict the postseason results to 2008: `FROM postseason AS T1 JOIN team AS T2 ON T1.team_id_winner  =  T2.team_id_br WHERE T1.year  =  2008`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group the results by winning team so each team's postseason victories can be counted: `FROM postseason AS T1 JOIN team AS T2 ON T1.team_id_winner  =  T2.team_id_br WHERE T1.year  =  2008 GROUP BY T1.team_id_winner`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I order the grouped teams by their victory counts in descending order, putting the team with the most victories first: `FROM postseason AS T1 JOIN team AS T2 ON T1.team_id_winner  =  T2.team_id_br WHERE T1.year  =  2008 GROUP BY T1.team_id_winner ORDER BY count(*) DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I project the team name and winner id, then keep only the first-ranked team: `SELECT T2.name ,  T1.team_id_winner FROM postseason AS T1 JOIN team AS T2 ON T1.team_id_winner  =  T2.team_id_br WHERE T1.year  =  2008 GROUP BY T1.team_id_winner ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1;`.

Question:
Among the employees who have a pay rate of above 40, how many of them are male?

Evidence:
pay rate above 40 refers to Rate>40; male employee refers to Gender = M
ground_truth.answer: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.Gender = 'M' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM EmployeePayHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.Rate > 40

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with the pay-history records, where each employee’s pay rate is stored: `FROM EmployeePayHistory AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join each pay record to its employee so the corresponding gender is available: `FROM EmployeePayHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I restrict the joined records to pay rates above 40: `FROM EmployeePayHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.Rate > 40`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I count the qualifying male records by summing 1 when the employee’s gender is M and 0 otherwise: `SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.Gender = 'M' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM EmployeePayHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.Rate > 40`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: This completes the count of male employees represented by pay records above 40: `SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.Gender = 'M' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM EmployeePayHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.Rate > 40`.

What is the average winning rate of the Buffalo Sabres in 2000?

DIVIDE(SUM(DIVIDE(W,G), COUNT(oppID) where year = 2000; Montreal Canadiens is name of team;
ground_truth.answer: SELECT SUM(CAST(T2.W AS REAL) / T2.G) / COUNT(T1.oppID) FROM TeamVsTeam AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.year = T2.year AND T1.tmID = T2.tmID WHERE T2.name = 'Buffalo Sabres' AND T1.year = 2000

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from `TeamVsTeam`, since each opponent row supplies the `oppID` count used to average the rate: `FROM TeamVsTeam AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join the matching team-season row to obtain Buffalo's wins, games, and team name: `FROM TeamVsTeam AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.year = T2.year AND T1.tmID = T2.tmID`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I identify the Buffalo Sabres by the team name: `FROM TeamVsTeam AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.year = T2.year AND T1.tmID = T2.tmID WHERE T2.name = 'Buffalo Sabres'`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I then restrict the opponent records to the 2000 season: `FROM TeamVsTeam AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.year = T2.year AND T1.tmID = T2.tmID WHERE T2.name = 'Buffalo Sabres' AND T1.year = 2000`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I calculate each joined row's winning rate as wins divided by games, cast wins to REAL for non-integer division, sum those rates, and divide by the opponent count: `SELECT SUM(CAST(T2.W AS REAL) / T2.G) / COUNT(T1.oppID) FROM TeamVsTeam AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.year = T2.year AND T1.tmID = T2.tmID WHERE T2.name = 'Buffalo Sabres' AND T1.year = 2000`.

prefix_hints.sol_3: I group the Massachusetts rows by zip code so each zip code's area codes can be counted: `FROM area_code AS T1 INNER JOIN zip_data AS T2 ON T1.zip_code = T2.zip_code WHERE T2.state = 'MA' GROUP BY T1.zip_code`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I retain only zip codes associated with more than one area code: `FROM area_code AS T1 INNER JOIN zip_data AS T2 ON T1.zip_code = T2.zip_code WHERE T2.state = 'MA' GROUP BY T1.zip_code HAVING COUNT(T1.area_code) > 1`.

Question:
What are the ids of all products that were either ordered more than 3 times or have a cumulative amount purchased of above 80000?
ground_truth.answer: SELECT product_id FROM Order_Items GROUP BY product_id HAVING count(*)  >  3 UNION SELECT product_id FROM Product_Suppliers GROUP BY product_id HAVING sum(total_amount_purchased)  >  80000

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with the product ids recorded in order items: `SELECT product_id FROM Order_Items`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I group the order items by product so each product's order occurrences can be counted: `SELECT product_id FROM Order_Items GROUP BY product_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I retain products appearing more than three times: `SELECT product_id FROM Order_Items GROUP BY product_id HAVING count(*)  >  3`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: For the alternative condition, I union those results with product suppliers grouped by product: `SELECT product_id FROM Order_Items GROUP BY product_id HAVING count(*)  >  3 UNION SELECT product_id FROM Product_Suppliers GROUP BY product_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I finish by retaining supplier-side product groups whose cumulative purchased amount exceeds 80000: `SELECT product_id FROM Order_Items GROUP BY product_id HAVING count(*)  >  3 UNION SELECT product_id FROM Product_Suppliers GROUP BY product_id HAVING sum(total_amount_purchased)  >  80000`.

Question:
How many people in Montenegro speaks Serbian?

Evidence:
Serbian is one language; Montenegro is a country located in Southeastern Europe
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.Percentage * T2.Population FROM language AS T1 INNER JOIN country AS T2 ON T1.Country = T2.Code WHERE T1.Name = 'Serbian' AND T2.Name = 'Montenegro'

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from `language`, where Serbian and its percentage are recorded by country: `FROM language AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join `country` on the country code so I can identify Montenegro and access its population: `FROM language AS T1 INNER JOIN country AS T2 ON T1.Country = T2.Code`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I restrict the language record to Serbian: `FROM language AS T1 INNER JOIN country AS T2 ON T1.Country = T2.Code WHERE T1.Name = 'Serbian'`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I then restrict the matched country to Montenegro: `FROM language AS T1 INNER JOIN country AS T2 ON T1.Country = T2.Code WHERE T1.Name = 'Serbian' AND T2.Name = 'Montenegro'`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I multiply the Serbian percentage by Montenegro's population to obtain the requested number of people: `SELECT T1.Percentage * T2.Population FROM language AS T1 INNER JOIN country AS T2 ON T1.Country = T2.Code WHERE T1.Name = 'Serbian' AND T2.Name = 'Montenegro'`.

Question:
What are the first name, last name and id of the player with the most all star game experiences? Also list the count.
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.name_first , T1.name_last ,  T1.player_id ,   count(*) FROM player AS T1 JOIN all_star AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id GROUP BY T1.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1;

prefix_hints.sol_1: I join each player record to that player's All-Star appearances using `player_id`: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN all_star AS T2 ON T1.player_id = T2.player_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I group the joined rows by player so each group represents one player's All-Star experiences: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN all_star AS T2 ON T1.player_id = T2.player_id GROUP BY T1.player_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I order the player groups by their row counts in descending order, placing the player with the most experiences first: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN all_star AS T2 ON T1.player_id = T2.player_id GROUP BY T1.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I retain only that highest-count player: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN all_star AS T2 ON T1.player_id = T2.player_id GROUP BY T1.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I project the player's first name, last name, id, and All-Star experience count to complete the query: `SELECT T1.name_first , T1.name_last ,  T1.player_id ,   count(*) FROM player AS T1 JOIN all_star AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id GROUP BY T1.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1;`.

What is the description and code of the type of service that is performed the most often?
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.Service_Type_Description , T1.Service_Type_Code FROM Ref_Service_Types AS T1 JOIN Services AS T2 ON T1.Service_Type_Code  =  T2.Service_Type_Code GROUP BY T1.Service_Type_Code ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_1: I link each service to its type so I can count how often every service type occurs: `FROM Ref_Service_Types AS T1 JOIN Services AS T2 ON T1.Service_Type_Code  =  T2.Service_Type_Code`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I group the matched services by service type code to form one frequency group per type: `FROM Ref_Service_Types AS T1 JOIN Services AS T2 ON T1.Service_Type_Code  =  T2.Service_Type_Code GROUP BY T1.Service_Type_Code`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I sort the service-type groups by their occurrence counts in descending order, placing the most frequently performed type first: `FROM Ref_Service_Types AS T1 JOIN Services AS T2 ON T1.Service_Type_Code  =  T2.Service_Type_Code GROUP BY T1.Service_Type_Code ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I retain only that highest-frequency service type: `FROM Ref_Service_Types AS T1 JOIN Services AS T2 ON T1.Service_Type_Code  =  T2.Service_Type_Code GROUP BY T1.Service_Type_Code ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I project both the description and code of the resulting service type, completing the query: `SELECT T1.Service_Type_Description , T1.Service_Type_Code FROM Ref_Service_Types AS T1 JOIN Services AS T2 ON T1.Service_Type_Code  =  T2.Service_Type_Code GROUP BY T1.Service_Type_Code ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.

ground_truth.answer: SELECT avg(T1.height) FROM player AS T1 JOIN player_college AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id JOIN college AS T3 ON T3.college_id  = T2.college_id WHERE T3.name_full  =  'Yale University';

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from `player` because each player's height is stored there: `FROM player AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I link each player to their college attendance records through the shared player id: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN player_college AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I then join the college details so the institution's full name is available: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN player_college AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id JOIN college AS T3 ON T3.college_id  = T2.college_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I restrict the matched records to Yale University: `FROM player AS T1 JOIN player_college AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id JOIN college AS T3 ON T3.college_id  = T2.college_id WHERE T3.name_full  =  'Yale University'`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I average the heights of the qualifying players: `SELECT avg(T1.height) FROM player AS T1 JOIN player_college AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id JOIN college AS T3 ON T3.college_id  = T2.college_id WHERE T3.name_full  =  'Yale University';`.

prefix_hints.sol_4: I retain customers whose count of distinct product ids is at least three: `FROM customers AS T1 JOIN customer_orders AS T2 ON T1.customer_id  =  T2.customer_id JOIN order_items AS T3 ON T2.order_id  =  T3.order_id GROUP BY T1.customer_id HAVING COUNT (DISTINCT T3.product_id)  >=  3`.

prefix_hints.sol_5: I also return the allergy description to identify what kind of allergy she has: `SELECT CASE WHEN SUBSTR(T1.STOP, -2, 1) != '9' THEN SUBSTR(T1.STOP, LENGTH(T1.STOP) - 1) + 2000 END - CASE WHEN SUBSTR(T1.START, -2, 1) = '9' THEN SUBSTR(T1.START, LENGTH(T1.START) - 1) + 1900 ELSE SUBSTR(T1.START, LENGTH(T1.START) - 1) + 2000 END AS years , T1.DESCRIPTION FROM allergies AS T1 INNER JOIN patients AS T2 ON T2.patient = T1.PATIENT WHERE T1.STOP IS NOT NULL AND T1.START IS NOT NULL AND T2.first = 'Isadora' AND T2.last = 'Moen'`.

Find the average height of the players who belong to the college called 'Yale University'.
ground_truth.answer: SELECT avg(T1.height) FROM player AS T1 JOIN player_college AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id JOIN college AS T3 ON T3.college_id  =  T2.college_id WHERE T3.name_full  =  'Yale University';

Question:
What is the total amount due of all the purchases made by the company to the vendor that has the lowest selling price amount of a single product? Indicate the name of the vendor to which the purchases was made.

Evidence:
Vendor's selling price of a single product refers to UnitPrice;
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T1.UnitPrice, T3.Name FROM PurchaseOrderDetail AS T1 INNER JOIN PurchaseOrderHeader AS T2 ON T1.PurchaseOrderID = T2.PurchaseOrderID INNER JOIN Vendor AS T3 ON T2.VendorID = T3.BusinessEntityID ORDER BY T1.UnitPrice LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from purchase-order line items because `UnitPrice` contains each product’s selling price: `FROM PurchaseOrderDetail AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I link each line item to its purchase-order header so I can identify the associated vendor: `FROM PurchaseOrderDetail AS T1 INNER JOIN PurchaseOrderHeader AS T2 ON T1.PurchaseOrderID = T2.PurchaseOrderID`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I then join the vendor record to obtain the vendor’s name: `FROM PurchaseOrderDetail AS T1 INNER JOIN PurchaseOrderHeader AS T2 ON T1.PurchaseOrderID = T2.PurchaseOrderID INNER JOIN Vendor AS T3 ON T2.VendorID = T3.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I sort the line items by unit price and retain the single lowest-priced one: `FROM PurchaseOrderDetail AS T1 INNER JOIN PurchaseOrderHeader AS T2 ON T1.PurchaseOrderID = T2.PurchaseOrderID INNER JOIN Vendor AS T3 ON T2.VendorID = T3.BusinessEntityID ORDER BY T1.UnitPrice LIMIT 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I return that lowest unit price together with the corresponding vendor name: `SELECT T1.UnitPrice, T3.Name FROM PurchaseOrderDetail AS T1 INNER JOIN PurchaseOrderHeader AS T2 ON T1.PurchaseOrderID = T2.PurchaseOrderID INNER JOIN Vendor AS T3 ON T2.VendorID = T3.BusinessEntityID ORDER BY T1.UnitPrice LIMIT 1`.

prefix_hints.sol_3: I group the matched rows by block code to form one result group for each code: `FROM BLOCK AS T1 JOIN room AS T2 ON T1.blockfloor  =  T2.blockfloor AND T1.blockcode  =  T2.blockcode GROUP BY T1.blockcode`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I count the joined room rows in each group and return the corresponding block code: `SELECT count(*) ,  T1.blockcode FROM BLOCK AS T1 JOIN room AS T2 ON T1.blockfloor  =  T2.blockfloor AND T1.blockcode  =  T2.blockcode GROUP BY T1.blockcode`.

Among the employees who were born before 1969, what is the work shift of the 6th oldest employee?

Evidence:
oldest employee born before 1969 refers to year(BirthDate)<'1969';
ground_truth.answer: SELECT T3.StartTime, T3.EndTime FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Shift AS T3 ON T2.ShiftId = T3.ShiftId WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.BirthDate) < '1969' ORDER BY T1.BirthDate LIMIT 5, 1

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with employees and link each one to their department history through the shared business entity id: `FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I then join the recorded shift so its working hours are available: `FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Shift AS T3 ON T2.ShiftId = T3.ShiftId`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I keep employees whose birth year is earlier than 1969: `FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Shift AS T3 ON T2.ShiftId = T3.ShiftId WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.BirthDate) < '1969'`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I order by birth date from oldest onward, skip the first five employees, and retain the sixth: `FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Shift AS T3 ON T2.ShiftId = T3.ShiftId WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.BirthDate) < '1969' ORDER BY T1.BirthDate LIMIT 5, 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I return that employee's shift start and end times: `SELECT T3.StartTime, T3.EndTime FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Shift AS T3 ON T2.ShiftId = T3.ShiftId WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.BirthDate) < '1969' ORDER BY T1.BirthDate LIMIT 5, 1`.
